clues.text: After Paul's ship broke apart, everyone aboard reached this island by swimming or clinging to planks.
As Paul laid sticks on a fire on this island, a viper fastened itself to his hand.
Islanders here showed Paul's shipwrecked group great kindness, lighting a fire because it was raining and cold.
Seeing a snake hanging from Paul's hand, the people of this island decided he must be a murderer.
When Paul did not swell up or drop dead after the snakebite, people here said he was a god.
Paul prayed and laid hands on the father of Publius, this island's chief official, healing his fever and dysentery.
Paul's company stayed on this island three months, then sailed on an Alexandrian ship that had wintered there.
